identification.summary: Winter Vivern is a cyber-espionage cluster that SentinelLABS says has targeted government organizations since 2021 [S3]. Proofpoint tracks the same activity as TA473 [S2], CERT-UA as UAC-0114 [S6], and Recorded Future as TAG-70 [S4]. It is a webmail-focused actor that has exploited Zimbra and Roundcube servers [S1][S2], and MITRE tracks it as G1035 [S7].
identification.firstObserved: SentinelLABS: targeting of government organizations since 2021 [S3]. Recorded Future: activity on behalf of Belarus and Russia since at least December 2020 [S4]. ESET's timeline shows Zimbra and Roundcube targeting since 2022 [S1].
identification.notes: Vendor names: Winter Vivern (DomainTools, Lab52, SentinelOne, CERT-UA usage per Proofpoint) [S2], TA473 (Proofpoint) [S2], UAC-0114 (CERT-UA) [S6], TAG-70 (Recorded Future) [S4]. ESET separately assesses a low-confidence link between Winter Vivern and MoustachedBouncer, a Belarus-aligned group [S1]; this is a vendor assessment, not a merge of the clusters. Microsoft has no name for this actor in the sources gathered.

attribution.sponsor: No government sponsor is publicly established in the sources gathered. Vendors describe activity aligned with Russian and/or Belarusian interests [S2][S3].
attribution.confidence: SentinelLABS states the group's activity aligns with the interests of the Belarusian and Russian governments [S3]. Proofpoint says TA473 operations align with support of Russian and/or Belarusian geopolitical goals [S2]. ESET assesses with low confidence a link to MoustachedBouncer, a Belarus-aligned group [S1]. Recorded Future describes the group as Russia-aligned and likely operating on behalf of Belarus and Russia [S4]. These are vendor assessments only; no government attribution was found.
attribution.basis: Targeting that tracks Russia-Ukraine war and European diplomatic interests [S2][S3]; CERT-UA and Polish CBZC technical sharing with SentinelLABS [S3]; tooling and infrastructure overlap assessed by ESET for the MoustachedBouncer link [S1].

objectives: Access to email of government, military and diplomatic organizations in Europe involved in the Russia-Ukraine war, per Proofpoint [S2]. Recorded Future reports intelligence gathering on military and political activity from email servers [S4]. Credential and session-token theft from webmail portals is the observed means [S2].

regions: Europe broadly, including NATO-related government webmail [S1][S2]
targeting.notes: SentinelLABS lists Polish government agencies, the Ukraine Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Italy Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and individuals in the Indian government among recent targets, plus a private telecom described as rare [S3]. Recorded Future reports more than 80 organizations, mainly in Georgia, Poland and Ukraine, between October and December 2023, plus Iranian embassies in Russia and the Netherlands and a Georgian embassy in Sweden [S4]. ESET reports Roundcube victims were European governments and a think tank [S1]. Proofpoint reports US elected officials and staffers were targeted in late 2022 phishing [S2].

capabilities.summary: Custom phishing sites and malicious documents tailored to targets, credential phishing, and exploitation of known vulnerabilities [S3]. Proofpoint reports scanning for unpatched webmail with Acunetix, exploitation of Zimbra CVE-2022-27926, and bespoke JavaScript payloads per target portal to steal credentials and tokens, with phishing sent from compromised accounts [S2]. CERT-UA reporting describes a lure imitating a Ukrainian Foreign Ministry site that delivered a fake antivirus scan and a batch file, leading to the Aperetif trojan [S6][S3]. ESET reports exploitation of Roundcube stored XSS CVE-2023-5631 as a zero-day starting 11 October 2023, requiring only that the message be viewed in a browser, with a JavaScript payload that lists folders and exfiltrates emails to C2; it also used older Roundcube CVE-2020-35730 [S1][S8]. SentinelLABS characterizes the group as resource-limited but highly creative, showing restraint in scope [S3].

campaigns.summary: ESET reports exploitation from 11 October 2023 against European government entities and a think tank, with email exfiltration; fixed in Roundcube 1.6.4, 1.5.5 and 1.4.15.

campaigns.summary: Recorded Future reports espionage against more than 80 organizations, mainly in Georgia, Poland and Ukraine, plus embassies.

diamond.adversary: Russia- and/or Belarus-aligned cluster of unknown sponsor; vendors differ on exact alignment [S2][S3][S1].
diamond.capability: Webmail exploitation (Zimbra CVE-2022-27926, Roundcube CVE-2023-5631 and CVE-2020-35730), tailored JavaScript payloads, phishing sites, and Aperetif [S1][S2][S3][S6].
diamond.infrastructure: Phishing domains imitating government sites, and C2 for email exfiltration; Aperetif beacons to a C2 domain per secondary reporting; Acunetix used for scanning; phishing sent from compromised accounts [S2][S1][S6].
diamond.victim: European government, military, diplomatic and think-tank webmail users; Georgia, Poland, Ukraine focus; US elected officials and staffers; embassies [S1][S2][S4].
diamond.socioPolitical: Collection of political and military intelligence relevant to the Russia-Ukraine war and European diplomacy [S2][S4].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing, unpatched open-source webmail (Zimbra, Roundcube) and users opening email in browsers [S1][S2].

gaps: No government attribution or sponsoring organization identified; vendor alignment statements differ (Russia, Belarus, Russia and Belarus) [S1][S2][S3].
Relationship to MoustachedBouncer is a low-confidence ESET assessment only [S1].

Full texts of ESET, Proofpoint, SentinelOne, DomainTools and Recorded Future reports could not be opened (fetch failed); details come from search-result summaries and secondary coverage, so confirm in primary reports.
DomainTools 2021 original report (reported to have first documented the cluster) not dated or verified here.
CERT-UA alert 5909 (1 Feb 2023) not opened directly; relied on SOC Prime coverage [S6].
No activity after early 2024 was found in searches; whether the group remains active in 2025-2026 is unknown.
Microsoft naming not found; Microsoft mapping not checked.
Post-compromise actions and downstream use of stolen email not described in sources gathered.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is internet-facing webmail (Zimbra, Roundcube) of government, military and diplomatic organizations, including coalition and allied partners [S1][S2]. STEP 2: The actor exploits known or newly disclosed webmail flaws and gains by slow patching; Zimbra's flaw was patched ten months before observed use [S2]. STEP 3: Template is scanning, then tailored phishing or XSS payload, then credential and token theft or email exfiltration [S1][S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued email collection against European and Ukraine-support government and diplomatic targets. MDCOA is use of stolen allied email or credentials to enable phishing of US personnel or to expose coalition planning; the US elected-official targeting shows US reach [S2]. Candidate indicators: Acunetix-style scanning of webmail, unexpected JavaScript or SVG content in inbound HTML email, webmail sessions exfiltrating mailbox contents to unfamiliar hosts, and lookalike government domains [S1][S2][S6].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track webmail CVE disclosures for partner and DoD-adjacent systems and share indicators from CERT-UA and vendors. (2) Authorities: coordinate any response on partner networks through host-nation and partner channels rather than assuming access. (3) Mission assurance: restrict public exposure of webmail, enforce patching and MFA, and treat allied email as potentially exposed during coalition planning [S2]. (4) Coordination: use allied CERT sharing, which enabled SentinelLABS discoveries, as the model for coalition reporting [S3].
